newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends up but off highs as longs exit.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends up but off highs as longs exit.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures mostly ended higher Wednesday in an active session, but most contracts closed well off the highs, hit by late profit taking after an early rally drove most of the board to new benchmarks.

June closed 4.4 cents higher at $2.353 per million British thermal units after rallying at midday to a new high of $2.43. July, which also set a new benchmark of $2.44, settled up 3.7 cents at $2.375. Most others also ended with gains.
While technical problems stalled the NYMEX after-hours ACCESS session, traders said Wednesday's AGA data was within expectations and should have little market impact.
"It (the AGA report) was a non-event. It does show people are injecting an awful lot of gas early which doesn't bode well for prices later in the season," said one Texas trader.

AGA said late Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks rose last week by 46 bcf, within the 40-50 bcf expected range, and were still 206 bcf, or 30 percent over year-ago. Eastern storage gained 28 bcf and remained 130 bcf, or 50 percent, over 1996 levels.

Traders agreed news of unexpected power unit outages at Entergy's 936 MW River Bend nuclear unit in Louisiana and at Arizona Public Service's 750 MW coal unit helped fuel the early drive to new highs today.
Weather forecasts this week remained mixed, with hot temperatures expected to persist in the West, while the East, Midwest and South should range from normal to below-normal.

Technically, traders now pegged resistance in June at the new high of $2.43 and then in the $2.47-50 area. Support was seen first at $2.20, with major buying likely at $2.05 and then along the up trendline around $2.04.

In the cash, Gulf Coast swing prices firmed 10 cents Wednesday to about the $2.30 area. Midcon pipes were up a similar amount to the $2.10-15 range. New York city gate gas firmed more than five cents to about $2.60.
The NYMEX 12-month Hub strip gained 2.2 cents to $2.386. NYMEX said 68,461 contracts traded, up from Tuesday's revised tally of 43,369.

On the KCBT, June finished five cents higher at $2.18, while deferreds ended steady to up by two cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.6 cents to 17.3 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 584 lots changed hands, up from Tuesday's total of 200.
